# Living World epic — implementation design

## Verified ground truth (corrections to the brief)

- Save schema is **v13**; the migration chain in `lib/game/save.ts` `readSave` runs v1→…→v13 and rejects unknown versions. `serialize()` (`GameEngine.ts:651`) writes v13 with **no `mobs` field** — mobs are session-only, confirmed.
- A new `MobKind` fills **six** exhaustive `Record<MobKind,…>` tables, not five: `MOB_TEMPLATES` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`), `MOB_DROPS` (`lib/game/mobLoot.ts`), `MOB_XP` (`lib/game/mobXp.ts` — the brief omitted this one), `CALL_INTERVALS` (`lib/game/audio/mobAmbience.ts`), `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS` + `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` (`lib/game/audio/soundParams.ts`). Plus a `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` membership decision (`lib/game/mobs.ts:122`). `soundParams.test.ts` iterates `MOB_TEMPLATES`, so all stay in lockstep.
- `MobState` (`lib/game/engine/state.ts:29`) has only `hostile: boolean` — no allegiance/owner today. Targeting in `mobAI.ts` is hard-wired to `state.player`.
- The renderer reconciles models **by `mob.id`** (`mobVisuals.ts:66`), and health bars are created only when `mob.hostile`. Restored mobs need no special re-attach: `sync` auto-creates a model for any unseen id.
- `removeMobAt` (`GameEngine.ts:822`) assumes the **player** killed: it routes drops to `state.inventory`, XP to the player, fires `mobDied`, and the boss-victory. The post-loop death sweep in `tickMobs` (`mobAI.ts:277`) calls it for **every** 0-hp mob regardless of cause.
- `WORLDGEN_VERSION = 8` (`config.ts:290`); worldgen PRNG decoupling pattern is real (`coalRand`/`dungeonRand` in `generation.ts`), and `collectDungeonSites` is the derive-pass precedent. BlockId enum ends at `Grindstone = 54`.
- `tame` items already exist: `bone` (`items.ts:123`) and `raw_fish` (`items.ts:166`).

---

## Recommended PR/commit breakdown (whole epic)

| PR | Phase | Save bump | Worldgen bump | Independently shippable & testable? |
|----|-------|-----------|---------------|--------------------------------------|
| **PR1** | 0b — Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat | none | none | **Yes** — hostiles now attack villagers; villagers flee. Pure-AI, user-visible, headless-testable with existing mobs. |
| **PR2** | 1 + 0a — Companions + mob persistence | **v13→v14** | none | Yes — tame wolf/cat, sit/follow/fight, persist pets. |
| **PR3** | 2 — Generated villages | reuses v14 (persist residents) | **8→9** | Yes — villages generate; residents spawn + persist. |
| **PR4** | 3 — Villager professions | **v14→v15** (additive `profession`) | none | Yes — profession-filtered trades + tint. |
| **PR5** | 4 — Raids | none (additive item id only) | none | Yes — raider mob + wave/trigger/reward. |

**Key sequencing decision (the cross-phase risk you flagged): split Phase 0.**
- **Phase 0b ships alone as PR1.** It is pure AI with no save impact, and it has genuine standalone value *using only existing content*: make `hostile` mobs target villagers (the `villager` kind already exists), and make villagers flee hostiles. That is shippable, observable, and headless-testable without any new mob — so it does not need to wait for Phase 1.
- **Phase 0a (persistence) folds into Phase 1 (PR2).** Shipping the v13→v14 bump on its own would persist *nothing* (no tamed pets, no residents exist yet), so it would be a save-version bump with no user-visible feature and nothing to gameplay-test. Folding it into Phase 1 ties the bump to the first thing worth persisting (tamed pets). Phases 2/3 then build on the v14 `mobs` field already in place.
- Risk if order changes: Phase 2's resident persistence depends on the v14 field from PR2. If Phase 2 must ship before Phase 1, move the v13→v14 mob-persistence bump into whichever PR lands first. Keep the order **0b → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4** and this never bites.

---

## PHASE 0b — Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat (PR1, no save bump)

### The allegiance model (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`)
Keep `hostile: boolean` (it is load-bearing for caps, `despawnHostiles`, `HOSTILE_CAP` directors, the snapshot `passiveCount`/`hostileCount`, and the health-bar gate). **Add a coexisting `faction`:**

```
Faction = "wild" | "hostile" | "ally" | "villager" | "raider"
```

Add to `MobState`:
- `faction: Faction` — set at spawn (`pushMob`) from a `FACTION_BY_KIND` map; overridden on tame (Phase 1) and for raiders (Phase 4).
- `owner?: "player"` — pet ownership (Phase 1; unused here but define the field now so the persistence shape is stable).
- `targetId: number | null` — session-only cache of the mob it is currently fighting.
- `retargetTimer: number` — session-only throttle for the enemy scan.

`hostile` stays the *threat/cap* axis; `faction` is the *targeting* axis. Initial mapping: sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig → `wild`; zombie/skeleton/spider/creeper/boss → `hostile`; villager → `villager`. (`ally`/`raider` arrive in later phases.) `pushMob` (`spawnDirector.ts:32`) sets `faction` from the map; `spawnBaby` (`breeding.ts:52`) inherits the parent's `faction`/`owner`.

### Shared target selection (`lib/game/engine/systems/mobAI.ts`)
One helper, `selectMobTarget(state, mob)`, driven by a small enmity table:

```
ENEMIES: ally → {hostile, raider}; hostile → {villager, ally}; raider → {villager, ally}; wild,villager → ∅
```

Behaviour: only "fighter" factions (`ally`/`hostile`/`raider`) scan. A fighter rescans only when `retargetTimer ≤ 0` **or** its cached `targetId` is dead/out of range — then one linear pass over `state.mobs` finds the nearest enemy-faction, alive mob within `detectRange`, reusing the existing scratch vectors (no allocation). Reset `retargetTimer` to `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS` (~0.6 s). This keeps the all-mobs loop **O(N)** per frame for steering and amortizes the O(N) scan to ~1–2 Hz per fighter, so worst-case stays well under budget for the ~70-mob population.

Player aggro is preserved as today for backward compatibility with every existing test: a `hostile` still prefers the player when the player is within `detectRange` (the existing `activeHostile` block). Only when no player aggro applies does it fall through to a mob target. A `raider` (Phase 4) inverts the priority (villagers first, player second). `villager`/`wild` never fight: villagers gain a *flee-from-nearest-hostile/raider* branch (mirror the existing animal-flee branch at `mobAI.ts:166`, but flee the nearest enemy mob instead of the player).

### Striking a mob target (not the player)
When a fighter is in melee reach + LOS of its `targetId` and `attackTimer ≤ 0`: lower `target.hp` by `attackDamage` (apply knockback to the target via the same `addScaledVector` pattern as `tryAttackMob`, `combat.ts:89`), emit `mobAttacked`, reset `attackTimer`. **Difficulty `dmgScale` is NOT applied to mob-vs-mob** — `mobDamageMultiplier` scales damage *to the player* only; mob-vs-mob uses raw `attackDamage`. Deaths are still handled by the existing post-loop sweep, never mid-loop (preserves the splice-safety invariant).

**Melee-only by design.** Ranged mob-vs-mob is explicitly out of scope: the projectile hit-filter is a binary `fromPlayer` flag (`projectileAI`/`state.ts:71`), so a mob arrow can only hit the player. Making arrows team-aware is a separate, larger change. Pets (Phase 1) and raiders (Phase 4) are therefore **melee fighters**. Call this out in the PR.

### Kill / loot / XP flow when a mob is the killer (`GameEngine.ts:822`)
Generalize `removeMobAt(index, opts?: { credit?: boolean; lootingLevel?: number })`, default `credit: true` so **every existing call site is unchanged** (player melee, arrows, spears, explosions, daylight burn all keep crediting). The death sweep in `mobAI.ts` computes credit from the **victim's faction**:

```
credit = victim.faction ∈ {wild, hostile, raider}   // false for {ally, villager}
```

Rationale: a pet (`ally`) killing a `hostile`/`raider` should still drop loot into your inventory and award XP ("your wolf hunts for you"), so a *victim-faction* rule (not attacker) is correct. A slain villager or pet yields the player nothing — and crucially closes the XP-leak where the player would otherwise farm XP off raiders/hostiles killing each other. (Today villager/ally drop tables are empty and XP is 0, so this is mostly a correctness guard, but it must be explicit before professions/raids give those factions value.) The boss-victory branch keys on `kind === "boss"` and is untouched.

### Save/worldgen impact
None. `MobState` is not serialized yet, so the new fields are session-only.

### Tests (headless `bun test`)
- `mobAI.test.ts`: spawn a zombie next to a villager → villager loses hp / flees; spawn far apart → no engagement; the enmity table and `selectMobTarget` as a pure unit. The credit rule: a hostile dying credits the player, a villager dying does not (assert no XP/loot delta).
- Regression: existing dawn-aggro-to-player tests stay green (player priority preserved).
- **Manual pass:** none strictly required (no visuals/audio change), though watching a zombie chase a villager is a good sanity check.

### Docs (PR1)
`docs/architecture.md` (allegiance model + the `removeMobAt` credit option), `docs/adding-content.md` ("A new mob" — note `faction` + the enmity table), `docs/testing.md` (new `mobAI` coverage row), `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## PHASE 0a + 1 — Companions + mob persistence (PR2, save v13→v14)

### 0a. Mob persistence

**What to serialize.** A minimal `SavedMob` carrying only irreplaceable identity/state; everything else is re-derived from the template:

```
SavedMob = { kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer? }
```

- **Persist:** `kind` (validated against a known-kinds set on load — drops unknown kinds for version drift), position (`x,y,z` floats), `hp` (finite, clamp to `(0, template.hp]`; ≤0 drops the mob), `faction`, `owner`, `sitting` (pet stay-state), and optional `ageTimer` (so a bred puppy stays a baby).
- **Re-derive from `MOB_TEMPLATES` on restore:** `speed`, `detectRange`, `attackDamage`, `attackCooldown`, `halfHeight`, plus fresh `direction`/`yaw`/`bobSeed`/`turnTimer`/`attackTimer`/`moveSpeed`.
- **Never persist (transient):** `fedTimer` (love window), `summonTimer`, `fuseTimer`, `targetId`, `retargetTimer`, `id` (fresh ids assigned on restore — see below).

**Minimal-persistence policy (recommended): persist only the `persistent` set — tamed pets ∪ village residents — NOT the whole population.** Justification:
1. Ambient wildlife and hostiles are *fungible* — `spawnInitialMobs` (`spawnDirector.ts:81`) re-seeds them every boot anyway, so persisting them is wasted bytes and would double the population on load.
2. It bounds the save: a save can't balloon with hundreds of wandering animals.
3. It avoids serializing volatile combat/AI state on throwaway mobs.
4. The boss and creepers are already deliberately transient (`fuseTimer`/`summonTimer`/`victory` never saved) — persisting a mid-fight boss reopens minion-cap and victory-flag hazards. Keep them transient, consistent with the existing design.

The persistence predicate is `isPersistentMob(mob) = mob.owner != null || mob.faction === "villager"`. In Phase 1 only pets match; Phase 2 marks village residents (also `villager`, so they match automatically).

**`serializeMobs` / `restoreMobs`** in `lib/game/save.ts` (mirroring `serializeContainers`/`readContainers`):
- `serializeMobs(mobs)` filters `isPersistentMob` and maps to `SavedMob`.
- `restoreMobs(save, surfaceYAt)` validates each entry, rebuilds a full `MobState` via a template-based factory (the same construction as `pushMob`), **re-grounds y** via `surfaceYAt(x,z) + halfHeight` (so a pet saved on now-air or buried terrain lands on the regenerated surface; `tickMobs` re-grounds every tick anyway), clamps x/z into world bounds (drop if hopeless), and assigns **fresh sequential ids** with `nextMobId` advanced past them. Fresh ids are safe because the renderer is a cold boot too (`mobVisuals` reconciles by id from empty).

**`migrateSaveV13toV14`** is a pure version bump (`mobs` absent ⇒ empty). `readSave` gains `if (migrated.version === 13) migrated = migrateSaveV13toV14(migrated)` and accepts `version === 14`. Types: rename current `SaveData`→`SaveDataV13`, add `SaveData = Omit<SaveDataV13,"version"> & { version: 14; mobs?: SavedMob[] }`.

**Engine wiring (`GameEngine.ts` constructor):** restore persisted mobs **before** `spawnInitialMobs` (line 286). `spawnInitialMobs` still runs unconditionally (it seeds fungible wildlife/hostiles at fixed counts, no cap check) so the world stays alive; restored pets/residents simply pre-exist. Cap interaction: `PASSIVE_CAP`/`HOSTILE_CAP` only gate *breeding* and *night/dungeon spawns* (both count live mobs), so a few extra restored mobs self-limit those — there is no crash and no runaway. `serialize()` adds `mobs: serializeMobs(state.mobs)`.

**Re-attach to renderer:** nothing special. On the next `renderer.sync`, `mobVisuals.sync` sees ids it hasn't created and builds models. Pets are non-hostile ⇒ no health bar (the existing gate). The pet's `owner`/`sitting`/`faction` drive an optional sit pose + collar tint (below).

**Edge cases (explicit):** unknown `kind` → dropped; non-finite/≤0 `hp` or non-finite coords → dropped; out-of-bounds position → clamped or dropped; mob on now-air terrain → re-grounded; version drift → migration + per-entry validation tolerate it.

### 1. Companions

**New `MobKind`s: `wolf`, `cat`.** Fill all six exhaustive tables + `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` (neither is hostile):
- `MOB_TEMPLATES` (`mobs.ts`): `wolf` small grey body / lighter head / dark legs, `speed ~1.3`, `hp 8`, `detectRange 0` (wild = passive wander), `attackDamage 4`, `attackCooldown ~0.9`. `cat` smaller orange-tabby, `speed ~1.4`, `hp 8`, `attackDamage 3`. (On tame, bump hp to a `PET_TAMED_HP` and set `detectRange` to `PET_FIGHT_RANGE` so the ally targeting engages.)
- `MOB_DROPS` (`mobLoot.ts`): `wolf: []`, `cat: []` (don't loot pets; wild ones drop nothing either — keep simple). `mobLoot.test.ts` allows empty tables.
- `MOB_XP` (`mobXp.ts`): `wolf: 1`, `cat: 1`.
- `CALL_INTERVALS` (`mobAmbience.ts`): `wolf [5,12]`, `cat [6,14]`.
- `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS` + `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` (`soundParams.ts`): wolf bark/growl ZZFX, cat meow/hiss ZZFX.

**Taming flow (reuse the feed plumbing, `interact.ts`).** Add `TAME_ITEMS: Partial<Record<MobKind,string>> = { wolf: "bone", cat: "raw_fish" }` and a `tryTameAimedMob(state, emit, rng)` mirroring `tryFeedAimedMob` (uses `findAimedMobIndex`, consumes one item via `adjustSlotCount`). On an untamed wolf/cat: roll `TAME_CHANCE` (config; 1/3 like MC); on success set `owner: "player"`, `faction: "ally"`, raise hp to `PET_TAMED_HP`, set `detectRange = PET_FIGHT_RANGE`, emit a new `mobTamed` event. On an already-owned pet, `tryToggleSitPet` flips `sitting` and emits a new `petSitToggled` event.

**Right-click precedence (`GameEngine.dispatch` `placeBlock`, currently `GameEngine.ts:538`):**
```
throw spear → tryTameAimedMob (wild wolf/cat + bone/fish) → tryToggleSitPet (own pet, non-feed hand) → tryFeedAimedMob (breeding) → tryTradeAimedVillager → tryInteractBlock → trySummonBoss → tryFish → tryUseHeldItem → place
```
Disambiguation: sit-toggle fires on your own pet when the held item is **not** the breed/tame food; with bone/fish on a *wild* wolf/cat it tames; with the breed food on two owned adults it breeds.

**Ally state machine (in `mobAI.ts`, the `faction === "ally"` branch):**
- `sitting` → fully parked (no follow, no wander, no fight; face forward).
- else if a valid enemy target in range (Phase 0b targeting) → engage + melee (credit-true kills feed the player).
- else if owner distance `> PET_FOLLOW_MAX` (~10) → steer toward the player; if `> PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE` (~24) → **teleport** adjacent to the player on solid ground (`surfaceYAt` + `collidesAt` check), mirroring MC wolf recall.
- else → gentle wander near the owner.

**Leverages Phase 0a** (pets persist: `owner`/`sitting`/`hp`/`faction`/position) **and Phase 0b** (ally targeting + the victim-faction credit rule).

**Breeding/drops.** Add `wolf`/`cat` to `FEED_ITEMS` for breeding; gate pet breeding on `owner` set. `spawnBaby` (`breeding.ts:52`) must **inherit `faction` + `owner`** from the parent so puppies/kittens are owned allies (they then persist). No drops while a baby (`ageTimer > 0`), already handled by `removeMobAt`.

**Procedural models / renderer (`mobVisuals.ts`, `mobModel.ts`).** New `MOB_TEMPLATES` `modelArgs` give wolf/cat their look via the existing `createMobModel` (body/head/legs/eyes/snout/stripe — no new geometry). Optional cheap visuals, read from `MobState`: tint the `stripe` material red for `owner != null` (a "collar"); lower the hindquarters / drop a leg rotation when `sitting`. Both are renderer-only reads of existing fields.

**New sounds/events.** `mobTamed` (happy chime + heart particles via `renderer.handleEvent`), `petSitToggled` (a soft yip/meow). Add the `GameEvent` variants in `state.ts`, route in `audioDirector.ts` `handleEvent`, and add a heart-burst case in `particleSystem.ts`.

### Save/worldgen impact (PR2)
Save **v13→v14** (additive `mobs?`). **No worldgen change** — wolves/cats spawn into the passive population via `spawnInitialMobs`; taming is interaction-only. `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays **8**.

### Tests
- `save.test.ts`: `migrateSaveV13toV14` pure bump; `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` round-trip; unknown-kind / garbage-hp / non-finite-coord dropping.
- `GameEngine.test.ts`: tame (seeded rng) → owner/faction/hp; sit toggle; follow (move player, step, assert approach); teleport when far; pet kills a spawned zombie and the player gets the loot/XP (credit rule); pet never targets the player; **persistence round-trip through a second engine** (pet restored with owner/sitting/hp; ambient wildlife not duplicated).
- `breeding.test.ts`: a bred pet inherits `owner`/`faction`.
- `mobLoot.test.ts` / `xp.test.ts` / `soundParams.test.ts`: auto-extended by the exhaustive Records (typecheck + iteration enforce wolf/cat rows).
- `mobVisuals.test.ts`: wolf/cat models build, dispose cleanly.
- **Manual pass (not headless):** wolf/cat appearance, collar tint, sit pose, bark/meow ZZFX quality, tame heart particles.

### Docs (PR2)
`docs/save-format.md` (v14 entry: `SavedMob` shape, persist-vs-transient policy, migration, edge cases), `docs/architecture.md` (persistence in serialize/restore; the ally state machine as a new `mobAI` behavior), `docs/adding-content.md` (a "Taming / companion mob" subsection; correct the table count to **six**), `docs/testing.md`, `docs/tuning.md` (`TAME_CHANCE`, `PET_*` distances/ranges, `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS`), `docs/manual.md` + `docs/reference.md` (taming, sit/follow), `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## PHASE 2 — Generated villages (PR3, WORLDGEN_VERSION 8→9) — sketch

**Seams.** Append a `placeVillages(world, cfg)` pass **last** in `generateWorld` (`generation.ts:157`, after `placeDungeons`), driven by a dedicated `villageRand(world.seed)` (like `coalRand`/`dungeonRand`) so it never consumes the shared `rand` stream — existing ores/trees/houses/dungeons stay byte-identical and only village bytes are new. Reuse `placeHouse` for the buildings; arrange `GEN.villageHouseCount` houses radially/grid around a validated flat center (validate against the seed-pure `terrainTopY`, like dungeons, and keep clear of spawn). Reuse existing blocks (cobblestone paths, planks, doors) — **no new `BlockId`** to keep the PR lean.

**Worldgen→mob seam.** Add a derive pass `collectVillageSites(world, worldType)` (the `collectDungeonSites` pattern: a `write/record` toggle over the shared placement routine, drawing a fixed number of values per village from `villageRand`). The engine stores `state.villageSites` (session, re-derived each boot) and spawns `GEN.villagersPerVillage` villagers at each site at boot, **flagged persistent** (`faction === "villager"` already qualifies under `isPersistentMob`). Reduce `spawnInitialMobs`' spawn-area villager count when village sites exist (cosmetic).

**Save/worldgen impact.** Any block write breaks the hash → **bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** and re-baseline the `generation.test.ts` SHA-256 digests + the in-region meshing snapshot in the same commit (per `docs/testing.md` case 1). Existing worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from seed (documented). Add a **structural probe** test (a village's houses generate; `collectVillageSites` reproduces centers; villagers spawn there) that survives re-baselining. Resident persistence **reuses v14** — no new save bump.

**Tests:** worldgen determinism re-baseline + structural probe; engine boot spawns residents at sites and they persist across reload. **Manual pass:** village layout aesthetics. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (WORLDGEN_VERSION 8→9 + residents reuse v14), `architecture.md`, `adding-content.md` (extend "A worldgen structure"), `testing.md` (re-baseline note), `tuning.md` (`villageCount`/`villageHouseCount`/`villagersPerVillage`), `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## PHASE 3 — Villager professions (PR4, save v14→v15) — sketch

**Seams.** Add `Profession = "farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric" | "none"` and a `profession?: Profession` on `MobState` (villager-only). Assign per resident at village spawn (seeded round-robin). In `lib/game/trades.ts`, tag each `TRADES` entry with a `profession` (a parallel `TRADE_PROFESSION: Record<recipeId, Profession>` map, so `Recipe` itself stays shared/untouched). `tryTradeAimedVillager` (`interact.ts:191`) sets `state.craftingStation = "villager"` **and** a new session field `state.activeVillagerProfession = mob.profession`. The "Trading" recipe-book category filters `TRADES` to the active profession; the `craft` command's station gate (`GameEngine.ts:404`) adds a profession check (spoof-guard) so you can't craft a blacksmith trade at a farmer.

**Differentiated look (renderer).** `createMobModelForKind` is per-kind, not per-instance. Add a per-instance recolor: `mobVisuals` reads `mob.profession` and recolors the villager's "smock" material (the `detail`/`body` material), exactly like `GameRenderer.setPlayerSkin` recolors named materials in place — zero new assets.

**Save/worldgen impact.** **No worldgen change** (profession is mob state). Save **v14→v15**: additive `profession?` on `SavedMob` — a pure version bump (`migrateSaveV14toV15`), validated against the known professions on load. `state.activeVillagerProfession` is session-only. (Alternative: pre-include `profession?` in the v14 `SavedMob` in PR2 to avoid a second bump — noted, but the one-feature-per-bump discipline favors v15.)

**Tests:** `trades.test.ts` (each profession's subset is a valid two-sided economy; the profession filter); engine (right-click a farmer shows only farmer trades; a blacksmith trade refuses while talking to a farmer); save round-trip of `profession`. **Manual pass:** profession tints. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (v15), `architecture.md`/`adding-content.md` (profession→trade-subset mechanism), `testing.md`, `manual.md`/`reference.md` (trades by profession), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## PHASE 4 — Raids (PR5, no save/worldgen bump beyond a new item) — sketch

# Living World — phased feature epic

## Context

The game has gone **deep on player-facing systems** (7 gear tiers, enchant/brew/anvil/grindstone/mending, XP, 4 game modes × 4 difficulties + hardcore, armor, advancements & stats) but the **world itself is static and lonely**: mobs never react to each other, biomes are visual-only, weather is cosmetic, villagers wander among generated "houses" with no real settlements, and *no mob is ever saved* (every creature is session-only, respawned from scratch each boot).

The user wants a **"Living World"** direction built from four reinforcing pieces — **generated villages + villager professions + raids + tameable wolf/cat companions that fight for the player** (essentially Minecraft's Village & Pillage + companion mobs). The pieces synergize: villages give raids a target, professions make villages worth defending, raids turn villages into stakes, companions help you survive.

This is a **3–4 PR epic** resting on two shared, currently-missing prerequisites: **mob persistence** and **mob-vs-mob combat (a third allegiance)**. The user chose to plan the whole arc now, with Phase 1 execution-ready and later phases sketched, then execute PR by PR.

All design claims below were verified against source. Project constraints hold throughout: **zero binary assets** (procedural models/sprites, ZZFX audio), one logical commit per slice, Conventional Commits, docs+tests+CHANGELOG ship *with* each change, and the full verify gate green before anything lands.

## Roadmap at a glance

| PR | Phase | Save | Worldgen | Ships standalone? |
|----|-------|------|----------|-------------------|
| **PR1** | 0b — Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat | none | none | Yes — hostiles attack villagers, villagers flee; pure-AI, headless-testable with existing mobs |
| **PR2** | 0a + 1 — Mob persistence + companions | **v13→v14** | none | Yes — tame wolf/cat; sit/follow/fight; pets persist |
| **PR3** | 2 — Generated villages | reuses v14 | **8→9** | Yes — villages generate; residents spawn + persist |
| **PR4** | 3 — Villager professions | **v14→v15** | none | Yes — profession-filtered trades + tint |
| **PR5** | 4 — Raids | additive item id only | none | Yes — raider mob + waves/trigger/reward |

**Sequencing decision (the key cross-phase call):** split Phase 0. **Phase 0b ships alone (PR1)** — it has standalone value using only existing content and no save impact. **Phase 0a (persistence) folds into Phase 1 (PR2)** — shipping the save bump alone would persist nothing (no pets/residents exist yet). Keep order **0b → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4** so each save/worldgen dependency is already in place when later phases need it. Two key technical limits, accepted for this epic: **mob-vs-mob is melee-only** (the `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` filter is binary — `state.ts:72` — so mob arrows can only hit the player; team-aware projectiles are a separate effort), and **difficulty `dmgScale` applies only to damage dealt *to the player*** (mob-vs-mob uses raw `attackDamage`).

---

## PR1 — Phase 0b: Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat (no save bump)

**Allegiance model** (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`, `MobState` at line 29). Keep `hostile: boolean` (load-bearing for caps, `despawnHostiles`, snapshot counts, health-bar gate). Add a coexisting targeting axis:
- `faction: "wild" | "hostile" | "ally" | "villager" | "raider"` — set at spawn from a `FACTION_BY_KIND` map.
- `owner?: "player"` — pet ownership (define now so the persisted shape is stable; used in PR2).
- `targetId: number | null` + `retargetTimer: number` — session-only targeting cache/throttle.

Initial mapping: sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig→`wild`; zombie/skeleton/spider/creeper/boss→`hostile`; villager→`villager`. `pushMob` (`spawnDirector.ts:32`) sets `faction` from the map; `spawnBaby` (`breeding.ts:52`) inherits parent `faction`/`owner`.

**Shared targeting** (`lib/game/engine/systems/mobAI.ts`). One pure helper `selectMobTarget(state, mob)` driven by an enmity table (`ally→{hostile,raider}`, `hostile→{villager,ally}`, `raider→{villager,ally}`, `wild`/`villager`→∅). Only fighter factions scan; a fighter rescans only when `retargetTimer ≤ 0` or its cached target is dead/out-of-range, then one linear nearest-enemy pass reusing existing scratch vectors. Throttle to `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS` (~0.6s) so steering stays O(N)/frame and scans amortize to ~1–2 Hz per fighter (safe for the ~70-mob population). **Preserve player aggro exactly as today** — a `hostile` prefers the player when in range (existing `activeHostile` block), falling through to a mob target only otherwise (keeps every existing test green). Villagers/`wild` never fight; villagers gain a *flee-from-nearest-enemy* branch mirroring the animal-flee branch at `mobAI.ts:166`.

**Striking a mob target.** In melee reach + LOS with `attackTimer ≤ 0`: lower `target.hp`, apply knockback (same `addScaledVector` pattern as `tryAttackMob`, `combat.ts:89`), emit `mobAttacked`, reset timer. Deaths still handled only by the existing post-loop sweep (`mobAI.ts:277`) — never mid-loop (splice-safety invariant).

**Kill credit** (`removeMobAt`, `GameEngine.ts:822`). Current signature `removeMobAt(index, lootingLevel = 0)` routes drops→`state.inventory` and XP→`awardXp` (player), hard-coding player credit. Generalize to `removeMobAt(index, opts?: { credit?: boolean; lootingLevel?: number })`, `credit` defaulting `true` so **all existing call sites are unchanged**. The death sweep computes credit from the **victim's faction**: `credit = victim.faction ∈ {wild, hostile, raider}` (false for `ally`/`villager`). Rationale: a pet killing a hostile *should* feed your inventory/XP ("your wolf hunts for you"); a slain villager/pet yields nothing, and this closes the XP-leak where mobs killing each other would farm player XP. Boss-victory branch (`kind === "boss"`) untouched.

**Save/worldgen:** none (new fields session-only). **Tests** (`mobAI.test.ts`): zombie-next-to-villager engagement; the enmity table + `selectMobTarget` as pure units; credit rule (hostile death credits player, villager death does not); existing dawn-aggro regressions stay green. **Docs:** `architecture.md` (allegiance + `removeMobAt` credit opt), `adding-content.md` (`faction` + enmity table), `testing.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## PR2 — Phase 0a + 1: Mob persistence + companions (save v13→v14)

### Mob persistence (Phase 0a)

`SavedMob = { kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer? }`. Re-derive everything else (`speed`, `detectRange`, `attackDamage`, `halfHeight`, fresh `direction`/`yaw`/`bobSeed`/timers) from `MOB_TEMPLATES`. Never persist `fedTimer`/`summonTimer`/`fuseTimer`/`targetId`/`id`.

**Policy: persist only the `persistent` set — `isPersistentMob(m) = m.owner != null || m.faction === "villager"`** (tamed pets ∪ village residents), NOT the whole population. Justification: ambient wildlife/hostiles are fungible (`spawnInitialMobs` re-seeds them every boot, so persisting would *double* them), it bounds save size, and boss/creepers are already deliberately transient. In PR2 only pets match; PR3 residents match automatically.

`serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` in `lib/game/save.ts` (mirror `serializeContainers`/`readContainers`): serialize filters `isPersistentMob`; restore validates each entry, rebuilds a full `MobState` via the template factory, **re-grounds y** via `surfaceYAt(x,z)+halfHeight` (handles pets saved on now-air/buried terrain), clamps/drops out-of-bounds, and assigns **fresh sequential ids** (safe — renderer reconciles by id from a cold boot). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure bump (`mobs` absent ⇒ empty); add `if (migrated.version === 13) … = migrateSaveV13toV14(...)` and accept `version === 14`. **Wiring** (`GameEngine.ts` ctor, ~line 286): restore persisted mobs **before** `spawnInitialMobs` (which still runs unconditionally to seed fungible mobs); `serialize()` adds `mobs: serializeMobs(state.mobs)`. Caps only gate breeding/night spawns, so a few extra restored mobs self-limit — no crash/runaway. **Renderer re-attach:** none needed (`mobVisuals.sync` auto-creates models for unseen ids; pets non-hostile ⇒ no health bar).

### Companions (Phase 1)

**New `MobKind`s `wolf` + `cat`** — fill all **six** exhaustive tables (the Plan agent corrected the count from five): `MOB_TEMPLATES` (`mobs.ts`), `MOB_DROPS` (`mobLoot.ts`, both `[]`), `MOB_XP` (`mobXp.ts`), `CALL_INTERVALS` (`audio/mobAmbience.ts`), `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS` + `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` (`audio/soundParams.ts`); neither joins `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS`. Wolf: grey body, `hp 8`, `attackDamage 4`, `detectRange 0` while wild. Cat: orange tabby, `attackDamage 3`. On tame, raise hp to `PET_TAMED_HP` and set `detectRange = PET_FIGHT_RANGE`.

**Taming** reuses the feed plumbing in `lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`. `TAME_ITEMS = { wolf: "bone", cat: "raw_fish" }` (both items already exist — `items.ts:123,166`). `tryTameAimedMob` mirrors `tryFeedAimedMob` (`findAimedMobIndex` + `adjustSlotCount`): on a wild wolf/cat roll `TAME_CHANCE` (~1/3); on success set `owner:"player"`, `faction:"ally"`, raise hp/detectRange, emit `mobTamed`. `tryToggleSitPet` flips `sitting` on your own pet (emit `petSitToggled`).

**Right-click precedence** (`dispatch`, ~`GameEngine.ts:538`): `throw spear → tryTameAimedMob (wild pet + bone/fish) → tryToggleSitPet (own pet, non-food hand) → tryFeedAimedMob (breeding) → tryTradeAimedVillager → tryInteractBlock → trySummonBoss → tryFish → tryUseHeldItem → place`.

**Ally state machine** (`mobAI.ts`, `faction === "ally"` branch): `sitting` ⇒ fully parked; else valid enemy in range ⇒ engage+melee (credit-true kills feed the player via PR1's rule); else owner distance `> PET_FOLLOW_MAX` (~10) ⇒ steer to owner, `> PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE` (~24) ⇒ teleport adjacent on solid ground; else gentle wander near owner.

**Breeding/drops:** add wolf/cat to `FEED_ITEMS`, gate pet breeding on `owner` set; `spawnBaby` inherits `faction`+`owner` so juveniles are owned allies (and persist). **Renderer:** wolf/cat via existing `createMobModel` `modelArgs` (no new geometry); optional cheap reads of `MobState` — red collar tint when `owner != null`, sit pose when `sitting`. **Events/audio:** add `mobTamed`/`petSitToggled` to `GameEvent` (`state.ts`), route in `audioDirector.ts`, add a heart-burst case in `particleSystem.ts`.

**Save/worldgen:** save **v13→v14** (additive `mobs?`), worldgen stays **8**. **Tests:** `save.test.ts` (migration; round-trip; unknown-kind/garbage-hp/non-finite dropping); `GameEngine.test.ts` (tame via seeded rng; sit toggle; follow/teleport; pet kills zombie → player gets loot/XP; pet never targets player; persistence round-trip through a second engine with no wildlife duplication); `breeding.test.ts` (inheritance); exhaustive-table tests auto-extend; `mobVisuals.test.ts` (models build+dispose). **Manual pass** (not headless): wolf/cat look, collar tint, sit pose, ZZFX bark/meow, tame hearts. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (v14: `SavedMob`, persist-vs-transient policy, edge cases), `architecture.md`, `adding-content.md` (taming subsection; fix table count to six), `testing.md`, `tuning.md` (`TAME_CHANCE`, `PET_*`, `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS`), `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## PR3 — Phase 2: Generated villages (worldgen 8→9) — sketch

Append `placeVillages(world, cfg)` **last** in `generateWorld` (`generation.ts`, after `placeDungeons`), driven by a dedicated `villageRand(world.seed)` (like `coalRand`/`dungeonRand`) so existing ore/tree/house/dungeon bytes stay byte-identical. Reuse `placeHouse` + existing blocks (cobblestone paths, planks, doors) arranged around a flat validated center (validate via seed-pure `terrainTopY`, keep clear of spawn) — **no new `BlockId`**. Add a `collectVillageSites` derive pass (the `collectDungeonSites` write/record-toggle pattern); engine stores session `state.villageSites` and spawns `villagersPerVillage` residents there at boot, flagged persistent (`faction === "villager"` already qualifies). **Bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9**, re-baseline `generation.test.ts` SHA-256 digests + meshing snapshot in the same commit (existing worlds discard stale diffs and reboot from seed — precedented), add a structural probe test that survives re-baselining. Residents reuse v14 — no new save bump. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (8→9), `architecture.md`, `adding-content.md`, `testing.md`, `tuning.md`, `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

`Profession = "farmer"|"blacksmith"|"librarian"|"cleric"|"none"`, optional `profession?` on `MobState` (villager-only), assigned per resident at village spawn (seeded round-robin). Tag trades via a parallel `TRADE_PROFESSION: Record<recipeId, Profession>` in `trades.ts` (leave shared `Recipe` untouched). `tryTradeAimedVillager` sets `state.craftingStation = "villager"` + a session `state.activeVillagerProfession`; the Trading recipe-book category filters to it; the `craft` station gate (`GameEngine.ts:404`) adds a profession spoof-guard. **Look:** per-instance recolor of the villager smock material in `mobVisuals` (the `setPlayerSkin` in-place recolor technique) — zero assets. **Save v14→v15** (additive `profession?` on `SavedMob`, pure `migrateSaveV14toV15`, validated on load); no worldgen change. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (v15), `architecture.md`/`adding-content.md`, `testing.md`, `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

`Profession = "farmer"|"blacksmith"|"librarian"|"cleric"|"none"`, optional `profession?` on `MobState` (villager-only), assigned per resident at village spawn (seeded round-robin). **New `MobKind` `raider`** (`faction:"raider"`, `hostile:true` so it counts against `HOSTILE_CAP` and Peaceful's `despawnHostiles` clears it) — fill the six tables + `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS`; melee (per the ranged-scope limit); target priority villagers→allies→player. **Trigger** via a craftable additive **"Ominous Horn"** item, used at a village — mirrors `trySummonBoss` (`GameEngine.ts:850`) as a `placeBlock`-precedence step (`tryStartRaid`), refusing if a raid is active. **Waves** in a new `systems/raid.ts` ticked after the spawn directors, reusing `tickBossSummon`'s cap/cadence guard; session-only `state.raid: { center, wave, totalWaves, raidersAlive, timer } | null` (transient like `state.victory`). content.text:
Honestly? For the **whole 5-phase epic**, one PR is too much — but you're right that five is probably too many. Let me explain the trade-off, because there's a clean middle.

**Why one PR for everything worries me:**
- It stacks **two save migrations (v13→v14→v15) and a world-invalidating worldgen bump (8→9)** into a single all-or-nothing merge. You couldn't ship companions without also shipping raids.
- The diff would be huge — a new mob-persistence serialization layer, worldgen structure generation + a hash re-baseline, **three** new mob kinds across six tables each, the raid system, and professions/trades. CodeRabbit and a human both review large diffs worse.
- If review finds a problem in raids or villages, your already-solid companion work is held hostage.
- Your own AGENTS.md frames a branch as landing "one reviewable unit" — a 5-phase epic is really five.

**Why five PRs is overkill:** the phases share so much foundation that splitting every one adds ceremony without isolating much.

**What I'd actually do — two PRs**, each one cohesive risk class, each with several focused commits (your usual style):

- **PR-A — "Living mobs & companions"** (Phase 0b + persistence + companions): pure behavior + save `v13→v14`, **no worldgen bump**. Allegiance/mob-vs-mob, mob persistence, tameable wolf/cat. Self-contained and low-risk.
- **PR-B — "Villages, professions & raids"** (Phases 2–4): the settlement cluster — worldgen `8→9` (the world-invalidating change, quarantined here), save `v14→v15`, raider mob + raids.

This honors your "few PRs, several commits" instinct (two, not five), keeps each review tractable, and crucially isolates the one change that throws away existing worlds. Within each PR, one commit per slice, lint green at every commit.

If you'd still rather do a single PR, I'd at least scope it to **PR-A only** and treat villages/raids as a follow-up — never the full epic in one merge.

Which delivery structure do you want? I'll update the roadmap in the plan accordingly.

# Living World — phased feature epic

## Context

The game has gone **deep on player-facing systems** (7 gear tiers, enchant/brew/anvil/grindstone/mending, XP, 4 game modes × 4 difficulties + hardcore, armor, advancements & stats) but the **world itself is static and lonely**: mobs never react to each other, biomes are visual-only, weather is cosmetic, villagers wander among generated "houses" with no real settlements, and *no mob is ever saved* (every creature is session-only, respawned from scratch each boot).

The user wants a **"Living World"** direction built from four reinforcing pieces — **generated villages + villager professions + raids + tameable wolf/cat companions that fight for the player** (essentially Minecraft's Village & Pillage + companion mobs). The pieces synergize: villages give raids a target, professions make villages worth defending, raids turn villages into stakes, companions help you survive.

This is a large epic resting on two shared, currently-missing prerequisites: **mob persistence** and **mob-vs-mob combat (a third allegiance)**. The user chose to plan the whole arc now and ship it as **two PRs** (see Roadmap) — Phase 1 execution-ready, later phases sketched. **PR-A is authorized to push + open; PR-B is built locally and held for the user's review before any push.**

All design claims below were verified against source. Project constraints hold throughout: **zero binary assets** (procedural models/sprites, ZZFX audio), one logical commit per slice, Conventional Commits, docs+tests+CHANGELOG ship *with* each change, and the full verify gate green before anything lands.

## Roadmap at a glance

**Delivery: two branches → two PRs, each with focused commits (one per slice), gate green at every commit.**

| PR | Branch | Commits (phase) | Save | Worldgen | Push? |
|----|--------|-----------------|------|----------|-------|
| **PR-A — Living mobs & companions** | `feat/living-mobs-companions` | c1 allegiance + mob-vs-mob (0b) · c2 mob persistence (0a) · c3 wolf/cat: tame/sit/follow/fight (1) · c4 docs/CHANGELOG | **v13→v14** | none | **Yes — push + open PR (authorized)** |
| **PR-B — Villages, professions & raids** | `feat/villages-professions-raids` | c1 generated villages (2) · c2 villager professions (3) · c3 raids (4) · c4 docs/CHANGELOG | **v14→v15** | **8→9** | **No — build locally, hold for user review before push** |

PR-A carries no worldgen change; **PR-B quarantines the world-invalidating `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9 bump**. PR-B branches off PR-A's merged `main` (it depends on PR-A's v14 `mobs` persistence field for village residents) — so **PR-A merges first, then PR-B**.

**Commit/phase order = dependency order** within and across PRs: 0b → 0a → 1 (PR-A), then 2 → 3 → 4 (PR-B). Persistence (PR-A c2) must precede companions and residents; villages (PR-B c1) must precede professions and raids. **Tests ship inside each feature commit** (mandatory to keep the gate green per-commit); **docs + CHANGELOG consolidate in each PR's final commit** along with that PR's e2e save/worldgen-version assert bump.

Two technical limits accepted for this epic: **mob-vs-mob is melee-only** (the `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` filter is binary — `state.ts:72` — so mob arrows can only hit the player; team-aware projectiles are a separate effort), and **difficulty `dmgScale` applies only to damage dealt *to the player*** (mob-vs-mob uses raw `attackDamage`).

---

## PR-A · c1 — Phase 0b: Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat (no save bump)

**Allegiance model** (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`, `MobState` at line 29). Keep `hostile: boolean` (load-bearing for caps, `despawnHostiles`, snapshot counts, health-bar gate). Add a coexisting targeting axis:
- `faction: "wild" | "hostile" | "ally" | "villager" | "raider"` — set at spawn from a `FACTION_BY_KIND` map.
- `owner?: "player"` — pet ownership (define now so the persisted shape is stable; used in PR2).
- `targetId: number | null` + `retargetTimer: number` — session-only targeting cache/throttle.

Initial mapping: sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig→`wild`; zombie/skeleton/spider/creeper/boss→`hostile`; villager→`villager`. `pushMob` (`spawnDirector.ts:32`) sets `faction` from the map; `spawnBaby` (`breeding.ts:52`) inherits parent `faction`/`owner`.

**Shared targeting** (`lib/game/engine/systems/mobAI.ts`). One pure helper `selectMobTarget(state, mob)` driven by an enmity table (`ally→{hostile,raider}`, `hostile→{villager,ally}`, `raider→{villager,ally}`, `wild`/`villager`→∅). Only fighter factions scan; a fighter rescans only when `retargetTimer ≤ 0` or its cached target is dead/out-of-range, then one linear nearest-enemy pass reusing existing scratch vectors. Throttle to `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS` (~0.6s) so steering stays O(N)/frame and scans amortize to ~1–2 Hz per fighter (safe for the ~70-mob population). **Preserve player aggro exactly as today** — a `hostile` prefers the player when in range (existing `activeHostile` block), falling through to a mob target only otherwise (keeps every existing test green). Villagers/`wild` never fight; villagers gain a *flee-from-nearest-enemy* branch mirroring the animal-flee branch at `mobAI.ts:166`.

**Striking a mob target.** In melee reach + LOS with `attackTimer ≤ 0`: lower `target.hp`, apply knockback (same `addScaledVector` pattern as `tryAttackMob`, `combat.ts:89`), emit `mobAttacked`, reset timer. ## Context

The game has gone **deep on player-facing systems** (7 gear tiers, enchant/brew/anvil/grindstone/mending, XP, 4 game modes × 4 difficulties + hardcore, armor, advancements & stats) but the **world itself is static and lonely**: mobs never react to each other, biomes are visual-only, weather is cosmetic, villagers wander among generated "houses" with no real settlements, and *no mob is ever saved* (every creature is session-only, respawned from scratch each boot).

The user wants a **"Living World"** direction built from four reinforcing pieces — **generated villages + villager professions + raids + tameable wolf/cat companions that fight for the player** (essentially Minecraft's Village & Pillage + companion mobs). The pieces synergize: villages give raids a target, professions make villages worth defending, raids turn villages into stakes, companions help you survive.

This is a large epic resting on two shared, currently-missing prerequisites: **mob persistence** and **mob-vs-mob combat (a third allegiance)**. The user chose to plan the whole arc now and ship it as **two PRs** (see Roadmap) — Phase 1 execution-ready, later phases sketched. **PR-A is authorized to push + open; PR-B is built locally and held for the user's review before any push.**

All design claims below were verified against source. Project constraints hold throughout: **zero binary assets** (procedural models/sprites, ZZFX audio), one logical commit per slice, Conventional Commits, docs+tests+CHANGELOG ship *with* each change, and the full verify gate green before anything lands.

**Delivery: two branches → two PRs, each with focused commits (one per slice), gate green at every commit.**

# Living World — phased feature epic

## Context

The game has gone **deep on player-facing systems** (7 gear tiers, enchant/brew/anvil/grindstone/mending, XP, 4 game modes × 4 difficulties + hardcore, armor, advancements & stats) but the **world itself is static and lonely**: mobs never react to each other, biomes are visual-only, weather is cosmetic, villagers wander among generated "houses" with no real settlements, and *no mob is ever saved* (every creature is session-only, respawned from scratch each boot).

The user wants a **"Living World"** direction built from four reinforcing pieces — **generated villages + villager professions + raids + tameable wolf/cat companions that fight for the player** (essentially Minecraft's Village & Pillage + companion mobs). The pieces synergize: villages give raids a target, professions make villages worth defending, raids turn villages into stakes, companions help you survive.

This is a large epic resting on two shared, currently-missing prerequisites: **mob persistence** and **mob-vs-mob combat (a third allegiance)**. The user chose to plan the whole arc now and ship it as **two PRs** (see Roadmap) — Phase 1 execution-ready, later phases sketched. **PR-A is authorized to push + open; PR-B is built locally and held for the user's review before any push.**

All design claims below were verified against source. Project constraints hold throughout: **zero binary assets** (procedural models/sprites, ZZFX audio), one logical commit per slice, Conventional Commits, docs+tests+CHANGELOG ship *with* each change, and the full verify gate green before anything lands.

## Roadmap at a glance

**Delivery: two branches → two PRs, each with focused commits (one per slice), gate green at every commit.**

| PR | Branch | Commits (phase) | Save | Worldgen | Push? |
|----|--------|-----------------|------|----------|-------|
| **PR-A — Living mobs & companions** | `feat/living-mobs-companions` | c1 allegiance + mob-vs-mob (0b) · c2 mob persistence (0a) · c3 wolf/cat: tame/sit/follow/fight (1) · c4 docs/CHANGELOG | **v13→v14** | none | **Yes — push + open PR (authorized)** |
| **PR-B — Villages, professions & raids** | `feat/villages-professions-raids` | c1 generated villages (2) · c2 villager professions (3) · c3 raids (4) · c4 docs/CHANGELOG | **v14→v15** | **8→9** | **No — build locally, hold for user review before push** |

PR-A carries no worldgen change; **PR-B quarantines the world-invalidating `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9 bump**. PR-B branches off PR-A's merged `main` (it depends on PR-A's v14 `mobs` persistence field for village residents) — so **PR-A merges first, then PR-B**.

**Commit/phase order = dependency order** within and across PRs: 0b → 0a → 1 (PR-A), then 2 → 3 → 4 (PR-B). Persistence (PR-A c2) must precede companions and residents; villages (PR-B c1) must precede professions and raids. **Tests ship inside each feature commit** (mandatory to keep the gate green per-commit); **docs + CHANGELOG consolidate in each PR's final commit** along with that PR's e2e save/worldgen-version assert bump.

Two technical limits accepted for this epic: **mob-vs-mob is melee-only** (the `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` filter is binary — `state.ts:72` — so mob arrows can only hit the player; team-aware projectiles are a separate effort), and **difficulty `dmgScale` applies only to damage dealt *to the player*** (mob-vs-mob uses raw `attackDamage`).

---

## PR-A · c1 — Phase 0b: Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat (no save bump)

**Allegiance model** (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`, `MobState` at line 29). Keep `hostile: boolean` (load-bearing for caps, `despawnHostiles`, snapshot counts, health-bar gate). Add a coexisting targeting axis:
- `faction: "wild" | "hostile" | "ally" | "villager" | "raider"` — set at spawn from a `FACTION_BY_KIND` map.
- `owner?: "player"` — pet ownership (define now so the persisted shape is stable; used in PR2).
- `targetId: number | null` + `retargetTimer: number` — session-only targeting cache/throttle.

Initial mapping: sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig→`wild`; zombie/skeleton/spider/creeper/boss→`hostile`; villager→`villager`. `pushMob` (`spawnDirector.ts:32`) sets `faction` from the map; `spawnBaby` (`breeding.ts:52`) inherits parent `faction`/`owner`.

**Shared targeting** (`lib/game/engine/systems/mobAI.ts`). One pure helper `selectMobTarget(state, mob)` driven by an enmity table (`ally→{hostile,raider}`, `hostile→{villager,ally}`, `raider→{villager,ally}`, `wild`/`villager`→∅). Only fighter factions scan; a fighter rescans only when `retargetTimer ≤ 0` or its cached target is dead/out-of-range, then one linear nearest-enemy pass reusing existing scratch vectors. Throttle to `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS` (~0.6s) so steering stays O(N)/frame and scans amortize to ~1–2 Hz per fighter (safe for the ~70-mob population). **Preserve player aggro exactly as today** — a `hostile` prefers the player when in range (existing `activeHostile` block), falling through to a mob target only otherwise (keeps every existing test green). Villagers/`wild` never fight; villagers gain a *flee-from-nearest-enemy* branch mirroring the animal-flee branch at `mobAI.ts:166`.

**Striking a mob target.** In melee reach + LOS with `attackTimer ≤ 0`: lower `target.hp`, apply knockback (same `addScaledVector` pattern as `tryAttackMob`, `combat.ts:89`), emit `mobAttacked`, reset timer. Deaths still handled only by the existing post-loop sweep (`mobAI.ts:277`) — never mid-loop (splice-safety invariant).

**Kill credit** (`removeMobAt`, `GameEngine.ts:822`). Current signature `removeMobAt(index, lootingLevel = 0)` routes drops→`state.inventory` and XP→`awardXp` (player), hard-coding player credit. Generalize to `removeMobAt(index, opts?: { credit?: boolean; lootingLevel?: number })`, `credit` defaulting `true` so **all existing call sites are unchanged**. The death sweep computes credit from the **victim's faction**: `credit = victim.faction ∈ {wild, hostile, raider}` (false for `ally`/`villager`). Rationale: a pet killing a hostile *should* feed your inventory/XP ("your wolf hunts for you"); a slain villager/pet yields nothing, and this closes the XP-leak where mobs killing each other would farm player XP. Boss-victory branch (`kind === "boss"`) untouched.

**Save/worldgen:** none (new fields session-only). **Tests** (`mobAI.test.ts`): zombie-next-to-villager engagement; the enmity table + `selectMobTarget` as pure units; credit rule (hostile death credits player, villager death does not); existing dawn-aggro regressions stay green. **Docs:** `architecture.md` (allegiance + `removeMobAt` credit opt), `adding-content.md` (`faction` + enmity table), `testing.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

120	 * advancements system to count hostile kills.
121	 */

124	/**
125	 * Body-center height above the ground for a mob kind. Mirrors the geometry
126	 * math in createMobModel so the headless simulation needs no Three.js meshes.
127	 */
128	export function mobHalfHeight(kind: MobKind): number {
129	  const bodyHeight = MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs[5][1];
130	  const legHeight = Math.max(0.3, bodyHeight * 0.56);
131	  return Math.max(bodyHeight, legHeight) * 0.5 + 0.2;
132	}
133	
134	/** Builds the Three.js model for a mob kind (renderer side). */
135	export function createMobModelForKind(kind: MobKind) {
136	  return createMobModel(...MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs);
137	}

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(mobs): allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat

Mob AI was strictly binary — passives flee the player, hostiles attack the
player, and nothing ever fights anything else. That makes the world feel
inert and blocks the upcoming companion/raid work, where pets must fight
hostiles and raiders must attack villagers.

Add a `faction` axis (wild/hostile/ally/villager/raider) to MobState,
coexisting with the load-bearing `hostile` flag (which still gates caps,
the health bar, and Peaceful despawn). `faction` drives a shared enmity
table and `selectMobTarget`: a "fighter" (hostile/ally/raider) locks onto
the nearest enemy-faction mob within detect range, re-scanning only every
MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS so steering stays O(N). Player aggro keeps strict
priority, so every existing dawn-aggro behaviour is unchanged. Villagers
now flee the nearest hostile/raider; wild animals still flee the player.

Mob-vs-mob strikes are melee-only (the arrow hit-filter is a binary
fromPlayer flag) and use the mob's raw attackDamage — difficulty scaling
applies to player-facing damage only. removeMobAt gains a `credit` flag
(default true, so every existing call site is unchanged); the death sweep
credits loot + XP by the victim's faction, so a pet's kill still feeds you
but a slain villager/pet yields nothing (also closing the XP leak of mobs
farming each other).

No save or worldgen change — the new fields are session-only for now
(persisted in the following commit).
EOF
